ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the first quadrant of the xOy coordinate plane, there exists a uniform magnetic field with its direction perpendicular to the coordinate plane and pointing inward. A positively charged particle with mass $m$ and charge $q$ is launched from point $M$ on the x-axis with an initial velocity $v_0$ at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ to the positive x-axis into the first quadrant. The particle undergoes circular motion in the magnetic field and then exits the first quadrant perpendicular to the y-axis. It is known that the length $OM$ is $L$, and the gravitational force on the particle is negligible.

1. What is the magnitude of the magnetic induction $B$ of a uniform magnetic field?
2. What is the time of motion of a particle in a magnetic field?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the first quadrant of the figure, multiple “×” symbols are drawn, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface and directed inward; among the coordinate axes, O is the origin, the x-axis points to the right, and the y-axis points upward. Point M is located on the positive half-axis of the x-axis, and the problem gives OM=L. The velocity v_0 emitted from point M points toward the first quadrant, and the angle with the positive x-axis is marked as 30°. The figure also shows that when the particle leaves from the y-axis, the velocity direction is horizontally to the left, that is, perpendicular to the y-axis. Reasoning: A positive charge in a magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface and directed inward is acted on by the Lorentz force, and the direction of motion deflects in the counterclockwise direction. The initial velocity direction makes an angle of 30° with the +x-axis, so the circle center C is on the direction passing through M and perpendicular to the initial velocity, that is, the direction making 120° relative to the +x-axis. Let the radius of circular motion be R, and take the coordinates of M as (L,0), then the coordinates of the circle center are C=(L+R cos120°, R sin120°)=(L-R/2, sqrt(3)R/2). The particle is emitted from the y-axis and the velocity is horizontal, so the radius there is vertical, and the x-coordinate of the circle center is equal to the x-coordinate 0 of the y-axis. Therefore L-R/2=0, obtaining R=2L. The radius of circular motion satisfies R=mv_0/(qB), so B=mv_0/(qR)=mv_0/(2qL). The particle velocity direction turns counterclockwise from the initial 30° to 180° when emitted, and the angle turned through is 150°=5π/6. The angular velocity is ω=v_0/R, therefore the motion time t=(5π/6)/ω=(5π/6)R/v_0=(5π/6)(2L)/v_0=5πL/(3v_0).
